proof_summary: Factoring the odd composite modulus as \(m=pv\), the case \(p\mid v\) is ruled out using the unit \(1+v\): since \(v^2=0\pmod m\), its power is \(1+nv\), and either permitted sign forces either \(p=2\) or \(p\mid n\), both impossible. When \(p\) and \(v\) are coprime, a hypothetical solution is combined by the Chinese remainder theorem with \(1\bmod p\) to produce a unit whose \(n\)-th power is \((1,-1)\), which is neither globally \(1\) nor globally \(-1\).
